subject: Discovery recap — Hyperscaler perf priorities & A/B test plan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Evan Santos <evan.santos@hyperdocs.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T16:20:00Z
Subject: Discovery recap — Hyperscaler perf priorities & A/B test plan

Evan — great call earlier. Summarizing the performance priorities we heard and a proposed A/B test approach so we can align on a short, measurable run: 

Priority summary (from your engineering lead):
- Primary: p95 latency at 512 tokens for user-facing calls (target <= 120 ms).
- Secondary: p99 latency (target <= 200 ms) and sustained tokens/sec under steady load (50-200 concurrent streams).
- Context window: 8k for heavier evaluation, 2-4k for day-to-day traffic.

Proposed A/B tests (quick, 48–72h runs):
1) Baseline: HyperDocs current hyperscaler endpoint (HYP-API) using your production prompt set (we need sample of 2000 calls).
2) Redwood-hosted: same model family (open-llm variant) served via Redwood hosted inference with default quantization profile.
3) Redwood-optimized: same model with our batching + prefix-KV cache enabled and tuned kernels.

Measurement plan (what we'll capture): p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, tail latency distribution, error rate, token cost per response. Please include the production prompt set and a shared-folder link for synthetic load (if you can share).

Action items for Evan: share a representative sample of 2000 requests (anonymized) and a short list of 3 API keys/endpoints we should use for the hyperscaler baseline. Link to drive would be perfect.

Internal asks (Neha / Rishi / Marissa):
- Neha: can you draft a bench-config.yaml (env, concurrency sweeps, warmup) and attach it to the run?
- Rishi: please reserve a Dedicated test pool for Apr 13–15 (4 A40-equivalent GPUs) and configure KV cache on by default for the optimized run.
- Marissa: prepare the benchmark-results-template.csv so the output is normalized across runs.

Attachments: initial-bench-hypotheses.md (short doc), call-recording-20270410.mp3

Thanks — Marcus
Redwood Inference | Enterprise Solutions
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Santos <evan.santos@hyperdocs.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Hyperscaler perf priorities & A/B test plan

Marcus / team — noted. Drafted a bench-config.yaml and attached for review. Key notes:
- Warmup: 500 requests at 32 concurrency, then linear ramp to target concurrency for each sweep.
- Sweeps: [8, 16, 32, 64, 128] concurrent streams for 512-token truncation, and a separate sweep for 2k token samples.
- Metrics: log token-emit timestamps for pXX calc, capture kernel selection histogram.

I recommend adding a short cold-start test (single request after 10m idle) to capture p99 tails — hyperscalers often optimize for steady state but tail matters for UX.

Attachment: bench-config.yaml (text)

Neha
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood
From: Evan Santos <evan.santos@hyperdocs.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T18:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Hyperscaler perf priorities & A/B test plan

Marcus — thanks for the clear plan. We're ready to move forward. I've uploaded a sample of 2,400 anonymized prompt/response records to the Drive folder and added three baseline endpoints in a secured note (sharing via the Drive permission): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-hyperdocs-bench-data

A few clarifications from our SRE: 
- Targets: p95 <= 120ms and p99 <= 200ms for 512-token requests (we understand these are aggressive against our current provider).
- Throughput: we expect 150 concurrent steady user streams (your sweep proposal covers this).
- Security: we'll want to see audit logs for the runs and short-lived test keys — can Redwood provide per-run ephemeral API keys and an events log?

We can start the first run on Apr 13. One ask: if Redwood's optimized run approaches p95 under the target but costs more, can you include an estimate of cost per 1k tokens for each run variant? That will be part of our procurement analysis.

Evan Santos
Head of Platform Engineering, HyperDocs
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Evan Santos <evan.santos@hyperdocs.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Hyperscaler perf priorities & A/B test plan

Great — thanks Evan. Quick alignment and owners + timeline: 
- Apr 12 (today): Redwood will provision ephemeral test keys and enable audit logging for the test project (owner: Rishi).
- Apr 13 00:00 UTC: Baseline hyperscaler run (Evan provides endpoints).
- Apr 13 12:00 UTC: Redwood-hosted baseline run.
- Apr 14 00:00 UTC: Redwood-optimized run (batching + KV cache).
- Apr 15: Normalize results, produce bench CSV and cost estimate per 1k tokens.

Owners: Rishi (test infra & ephemeral keys), Neha (bench config and run orchestration), Marissa (results normalization & cost calc). I attached the benchmark-results-template.csv — please use it verbatim so the procurement team can compare apples-to-apples.

Related links: HubSpot deal RDW-2027-HYP-0410 (please add any notes there).

Next immediate asks for Evan: confirm Apr 13 start window and grant Drive access to marcus.lin@redwood.com + rishi.malhotra@redwood.com.

Attachments: benchmark-results-template.csv

Thanks — Marcus
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
